m2c/tests/sandbox/test_net_probe.py -- Patch C11b: the network self-test (``probe.run_network_probe``), without bubblewrap.

The probe starts a REAL host-side proxy with a fake resolver, a loopback fake upstream and the test-only loopback flag,
then runs one sandboxed command and judges it from what that command printed AND what the host saw.  Here the "sandbox"
is a fake runner that EMULATES the in-sandbox client (it talks to the proxy's unix socket from the host, with the real
client text), so the verdict logic runs for real: every check passes with the emulation, and each failure mode is
produced by a variant of it.  The real thing is in test_net_real_sandbox.py.

Also pinned: the main probe's ``CHECK_NAMES`` and ``works`` are untouched, results hold fixed text only, the cache, and
cleanup (proxy stopped, directory gone, fake upstream closed).

Place this file at: m2c/tests/sandbox/test_net_probe.py

m2c/tests/sandbox/test_netbridge.py -- Patch C11b: the bridge (m2c.sandbox.bridge), module part and script part.

The script part is run for real as a subprocess on the host (no sandbox needed): it must bind, relay between a TCP
connection and a unix socket, and then ``exec`` the command so that the command's own exit status and signals are what
the caller sees.  If the bridge cannot be set up the command must STILL run (without network).  The module part builds
the proxy environment: injected after sanitizing, upper and lower case, with an EMPTY NO_PROXY, replacing whatever the
host had.

m2c/tests/sandbox/test_netproxy.py -- Patch C11b: the host-side proxy, against a fake resolver and a fake upstream.

Nothing here touches the internet: the resolver is a dict, the "upstream" is an echo server on loopback that the fake
connector reaches no matter what address the proxy pinned (the pinned address is RECORDED, which is the evidence).

What is proven: a denied or unlisted host is never resolved or connected to; private, loopback, link-local/metadata,
CGNAT, unique-local, multicast, reserved and IPv4-mapped destinations are refused even for allowlisted names; DNS is
resolved ONCE and the connection goes to that address (rebinding); one bad address in an answer refuses the whole
answer; plain http and non-CONNECT requests are refused with fixed text; oversized request lines and headers, slow
heads and idle tunnels are cut; connection caps hold; shutdown closes everything and removes the directory; the
test-only loopback flag is reachable from no setting, environment variable or production constructor.

Place this file at: m2c/tests/sandbox/test_netproxy.py

m2c/tests/sandbox/test_sandbox_doctor.py -- Patch C11a: what ``m2c doctor`` says about the sandbox.

The doctor's bubblewrap line used to mean "the program is on PATH".  Now, when it is, the doctor runs the sandbox
self-test and the line says the truth: ok (with how many checks passed), or a warning naming exactly which check failed
or why the sandbox cannot be built.  These tests drive the check with fake probe results through ``Environment.
sandbox_probe`` (no bubblewrap needed) and, where bubblewrap works, with the real one.

Pinned: a sandbox that does not work is NEVER "ok"; a probe that crashes is not "ok" either; the line stays a warning
(never a failure: m2c still runs without a sandbox, with its warning); the hints are specific; nothing in the text is a
path of the throw-away world.

Run: cd m2c && pytest tests/sandbox/test_sandbox_doctor.py -v -rs

m2c/tests/sandbox/test_sandbox_escape.py -- Patch C11a: real escape attempts against the real bubblewrap.

Every test here runs a command through the shell tool in ``sandbox="required"`` mode (so a missing sandbox is an
error, never an unsandboxed run) and checks TWO things, because a command can lie or fail quietly:
what the command saw, and what is on the real disk or in the real process table afterwards.

The world: a fake home (``$HOME`` is the suite's temporary home) with canaries in ``~/.ssh``, ``~/.aws``,
``~/.config`` and ``~/.m2c``, a project inside it with ``.git``, ``.m2c`` and shell rc files, and an "outside"
directory under ``/var/tmp`` that the sandbox does not mount.  Every canary is built at run time.

These tests need bubblewrap and user namespaces.  When they are missing every test is SKIPPED with a loud
"SKIPPED: <reason>" line on stderr (and the reason in pytest's -rs summary); nothing here silently passes.

Run (Ubuntu / WSL2 Ubuntu):   sudo apt install bubblewrap && cd m2c && pytest tests/sandbox -v -rs

What is NOT proved here, on purpose: bubblewrap itself and the kernel are trusted.  A kernel exploit, a
vulnerable ``bwrap`` or a command that abuses the project directory (it IS writable) is outside this patch.

m2c/tests/sandbox/test_sandbox_probe.py -- Patch C11a: the sandbox self-test (``m2c.sandbox.probe``).

Two halves.

1. Logic, with a FAKE runner (no bubblewrap needed, runs everywhere).  ``FakeSandbox`` behaves like a
   correct sandbox: it answers each check's script the way a sandbox that held would (and makes the one
   host-side change the "basic" check expects).  Every failure mode is then one deliberate deviation:
   a leak on the real disk, a leak in the output, a sandbox that does not start (each classified error),
   a hang, a crash, a missing binary, a refused profile.  What is pinned: the probe says "does not work"
   in every one of them and says WHICH check, the result never contains a path or output, the temporary
   world is always removed, and nothing is logged but words and codes.

2. The probe against the REAL bubblewrap, weakened on purpose (marked ``real_sandbox``; skipped loudly
   when bubblewrap or user namespaces are missing).  A probe that passes proves little unless it also
   fails when the sandbox is weak, so each mutation removes one protection from the real command line
   and the matching check, and only that one, must fail.

Run: cd m2c && pytest tests/sandbox/test_sandbox_probe.py -v -rs

m2c/tests/sandbox/test_sandbox_shell_regression.py -- Patch C11a: the shell tool behaves the same with the sandbox on and off.

C11a changes WHERE a command runs, not how a call is supervised: the timeout, the process-group kill, cancel, streaming and
the output cap are C07's, and the claim of this patch is that they are untouched.  This file is the evidence.  Every test here
runs the SAME assertions twice:

``unsandboxed``  ``ShellConfig(sandbox="off")``: C07's own path.
``sandboxed``    ``ShellConfig(sandbox="required")`` against the real bubblewrap (the ``real_sandbox`` marker; skipped LOUDLY
                 -- "SKIPPED: <reason>" on stderr -- where bubblewrap or user namespaces are not available, so a machine
                 without them never reports this as a pass).

Why these tests exist besides tests/tools/test_tools_shell.py.  That file's process tests write ``$!`` to a file and then look
at that PID on the HOST.  Inside the sandbox's PID namespace the number means something else, so under
``M2C_TEST_SANDBOX=real`` those six tests are skipped there (their ``skipif`` says so) and are replaced by the tests below,
which find the processes by a UNIQUE ARGUMENT (``sleep 3900.123456``) on the host's own ``/proc`` and ask the command itself
for positive evidence that its processes were running (``RUNNING:<n>``) before they were killed, so "nothing is left" can
